newsitem.title: USA: Nextel sees digital growth ahead of plan.
newsitem.headline: Nextel sees digital growth ahead of plan.

text.p: Nextel Communications Inc.'s new national digital wireless network is attracting users much faster than people who follow the industry had expected, the company said Thursday.

Speaking at a PaineWebber technology conference, Nextel President Timothy Donahue said that the success of Nextel's business-oriented digital network leads him to believe that the company's financial results will improve ahead of schedule.
McLean, Va.-based Nextel's stock was the second most active on Nasdaq, rising $1.625 to $16.375.

Nextel has an integrated wireless communications system that includes phone service, paging and voice mail. The digital wireless service offers higher voice quality than traditional cellular phones, and an innovative feature that allows a user to instantly contact any number of colleagues at the push of a button.
Driving demand is the 10 cents-a-minute charge for this direct connection, two-way radio service. In addition, the company has eliminated roaming charges throughout its national network.
Donahue said the Nextel digital network is growing in excess of the 150,000 net new subscribers Wall Street analysts have forecast for the current quarter ending in June.
"I will tell you that we will exceed that in the second quarter," he said.
By contrast, the company added 122,000 users in the first quarter, ending the period with 422,900 subscribers. The company's older analogue wireless network has about 700,000 users.
Donahue attributed the accelerating growth, in part, to a national $35 million TV, radio and print advertising campaign the company launched in early April.
"We had a hell of a first quarter and we are going to have a hell of a second quarter," he said.

Nextel reported first-quarter revenues of $111 million, versus $68 million in the year-ago period. But its net loss widened to $221 million, or 93 cents a share, versus a loss of $119 million, or 56 cents a share, a year earlier.

Donahue said he sees the company becoming cash-flow positive in the third quarter of 1998, ahead of the company's original plan to achieve that in 1999. But he cautioned that if the company changes course and begins to target the consumer market and not just corporate customers, the turning point in cash flow could be delayed.
He said the company has no plans to enter the U.S. consumer market because costs are prohibitive.
The company launched its Dallas operation Wednesday and now covers nine of the top 10 U.S. markets.
Nextel, backed by cellular pioneer Craig McCaw and Motorola Inc., has arranged $3 billion to fund the rapid expansion of its U.S. wireless operation.
